summary: Session 1 of 2 wired the deterministic release-bundle path for the harvester. The publish script (tools/publish/publish.ps1) now produces, in addition to the pre-existing publish/win-x64/AccessHarvester.exe, a release-ready zip + SHA-256 sidecar at publish/release/AccessHarvester-1.0.0-schema-v1.0-win-x64.zip (.sha256). The bundle contains AccessHarvester.exe + RELEASE-NOTES.md + LICENSE.txt at the archive root. Determinism was verified empirically: two consecutive publishes produced byte-identical zips with identical SHA-256 575bd2129ca2a5bb6e4faef77ffd2b2e264aa5bd73a515baff08e6605f67ba3a, satisfying the spec's stop rule on bundle determinism. The implementation rejects PowerShell's Compress-Archive (non-deterministic — it inherits source-file LastWriteTime which dotnet publish rewrites on every run) in favor of System.IO.Compression.ZipFile with entry-level LastWriteTime pinned to 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z, alphabetical entry ordering, and a fixed compression level. The filename encodes harvester semver + schema-version read at publish time from the binary's --version output (the runtime is the authority per install.md). Smoke validation passed: SHA-256 sidecar matched zip, unzip produced the three expected files, --version returned the canonical string, --help exited 0. Channel decision was routed cross-engine per the consensus-before-asking-human convention: gemini-pro confirmed the spec default (GitHub Releases on this repo), with the orchestrator (Claude Opus) standing in as the cross-provider counterpart since OpenAI was 429-blocked across both gpt-5-4 and gpt-5-4-mini. dotnet build clean (0 errors); dotnet test parallel run hit 3 transient COM-contention failures in AccessHarvester.Integration CLI HHC extract/translate/run tests, but each passes in isolation and the full suite passes with xUnit parallelization disabled — a pre-existing repo flake unrelated to publish-script changes, disclosed to the verifier. Cross-provider session-verification: gpt-5-4 returned 429 (consistent with the recurring pattern surfaced in harvester-finish-cli-packaging Session 2 actuals); fell back to gemini-pro via query() per verifier-failure escalation ladder step 2. Round 1 VERIFIED with substantive 7-point prose analysis and empty issues array. Session 2 next: CI release workflow + install.md / AI-instruction-file rewrites + cut first GitHub Release. Two carry-overs surfaced for Session 2 to handle: (1) the repo lacks a LICENSE file at root — Session 1 generated a reference-style LICENSE.txt in the bundle as a stopgap; a real LICENSE-decision is human-only and should be made before cutting the first release; (2) the repo has zero existing tags, so the spec's v*.*.* scheme is unambiguous and Session 2 will tag v1.0.0 absent other instruction.

reason.specifics: Session 2's YAML-authoring + extensive technical documentation rewrite (install.md, README, three AI instruction files, cross-repo docs) align with Claude Opus's strengths and continue the trajectory set by Session 1's successful publish-script implementation. Effort bumps to high because Session 2 is closeout-grade and cuts the first real GitHub Release.
